subject: Pricing structure and security gating for volume discounts
messages:
From: Anna Kline <anna.kline@finboard.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing and commitment tiers — SOC2 / DPA question

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this. A quick intro: I run platform decisions at FinBoard — we're evaluating Redwood for models behind several customer-facing features. We expect initial usage in the 20–60M tokens/month range and a steep growth profile.

We have two specific asks before procurement will move forward:
- Clear per-token pricing by commit tier (and how overage is handled)
- Confirmation of what security/compliance evidence is required to lock in any volume/commit discounts (procurement insists on DPA + SOC2 evidence).

Is the SOC2 report required up-front to get the committed discount applied, or can we sign the commit and provide SOC2/DPA within a short window? If the latter, do you apply discounts retroactively? Also please share an example term sheet so our legal team can review.

Appreciate a quick gut-check — procurement is on a tight 2–3 week timeline.

Best,
Anna
Anna Kline
Head of Platform
FinBoard Inc.

--
Attachment: none
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-10T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing and commitment tiers — SOC2 / DPA question

Hi Anna — thanks, and great to hear about the expected runway. Short answers up front:
- We price hosted API usage per-token with tiered commit discounts.
- An executed DPA and acceptable SOC2 evidence are required before the committed discount is formally applied to invoices.

That said, we commonly do a couple of things to help procurement move quickly:
- Provide provisional pricing and a term sheet while your legal review runs.
- Offer a short-term interim credit or provisional discount window that becomes permanent once SOC2 + DPA are verified.

High-level example (provisional):
- No commit: $0.00060 / token (standard list)
- Tier 1 (10M monthly commit): 12% discount -> $0.000528 / token
- Tier 2 (50M monthly commit): 24% discount -> $0.000456 / token
- Tier 3 (200M monthly commit): 36% discount -> $0.000384 / token
- Overage: Billed at list rate, with option to convert to higher tier if sustained.

Security gating specifics: we require one of the following before applying the committed discount retroactively:
- SOC2 Type II report covering the Redwood service within last 12 months, OR
- SOC2 Type II in progress plus a formalized remediation plan and bridge evidence (rare), OR
- ISO27001 certificate + audit report in lieu (case-by-case).

We will send a redlined DPA (standard Redwood DPA_v3) and a pricing term sheet for you to share with legal. If you'd like, we can also open a secure upload link for the SOC2 report and route it to our compliance team.

I'm attaching a provisional term sheet and a simple pricing model so you can run numbers. Sergio (cc) is your AE and will coordinate the procurement path.

Next steps:
1) I'll send the DPA and term sheet.
2) If you can share SOC2 evidence to the secure link, our compliance team will confirm and we can backdate the discount to the first invoice after verification.
3) If SOC2 will take time, we can apply a 30-day interim credit to approximate the discounted savings while your teams complete docs.

Would you prefer DocuSign for the DPA or an initial PDF for internal legal review?

Cheers,
Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--

Subject: Re: FW: Pricing and commitment tiers — FinBoard (need legal take)

Jonas / team — quick legal/compliance take:
- We should require an executed DPA before any committed pricing is applied. That can be a standard DocuSign flow.
- For SOC2 evidence: SOC2 Type II report within the last 12 months is preferred. If they only have Type I or an ongoing Type II, we can consider a 30-day provisional credit but: the customer must upload the report to our secure portal and agree to allow our compliance team to review before credits convert to permanent discounts.
- If they cannot produce SOC2 within 30 days, the provisional credit will be removed and billing re-calculated to list rates for the interim.
- Exceptions (ISO27001) will be reviewed but require case-by-case sign-off from Security.

Commercial note: offering 30 days of an equivalent discount (applied as a one-time credit) is reasonable and helps procurement timelines without binding Redwood.

I'll prepare a short DPA cover email and a checklist for SOC2 upload. Sergio — coordinate if you want legal to pre-fill specific clauses.

Vivek
Chief Legal Officer (acting)

Subject: Proposed pricing & next steps (DPA + SOC2 flow)

Hi Anna — following up with a concrete proposal and the process to get you to committed pricing quickly.

Proposed hosted-API commit (12-month term):
- Baseline list: $0.00060 / token
- 10M/mo commit: 12% off -> $0.000528 / token
- 50M/mo commit: 24% off -> $0.000456 / token
- 200M/mo commit: 36% off -> $0.000384 / token
- Overage billed monthly at list; if sustained, we recommend moving to a higher tier (we can automate true-up).

Security gating & timeline:
- Step 1: FinBoard legal signs Redwood_DPA_v3 via DocuSign (link below).
- Step 2: FinBoard uploads SOC2 Type II report to our secure upload link. Our compliance team will confirm within 3 business days.
- Step 3: Once DPA executed and SOC2 verified, we will apply the committed discount retroactively to the invoice cycle that starts after verification.

Interim option (to help procurement):
- If FinBoard needs discounts applied while legal/compliance are finalizing, we will grant a one-time provisional credit equal to 30 days of the committed discount. The credit converts to permanent billing discounts only after SOC2 + DPA verification. If evidence is not provided within 30 days, provisional credit is reversed.

Links & attachments:
- DocuSign DPA: https://redwood.app/docusign/FD-2026-089
- Secure SOC2 upload instructions: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/finboard/soc2-upload-instructions
- Attached: redwood_pricing_term_sheet_v1.pdf and pricing_model_example.xlsx that show sample monthly costs at different usage curves.

Please let me know which commit tier you want to target (we can always re-evaluate at quarterly business reviews). If procurement prefers, we can open a short window to sign the DPA and apply the interim credit immediately.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps move legal along.

Best regards,
Jonas
Redwood Inference

Jonas — thanks for the clear proposal and the interim credit option. Procurement confirmed they will execute the DPA via DocuSign this week. Two quick clarifications before we route the SOC2 document:

1) Upload method: is the Drive link the preferred route? We need an SFTP or an encrypted upload option that stays inside FinBoard's transfer policies (we can use your secure portal — please confirm the exact URL and contact).
2) Retroactivity: you note the discount is applied to the invoice cycle after verification. Can you confirm the discount is back-applied to usage from the contract start date OR only to invoices after verification? Procurement prefers backdating to contract start.

Assuming we get those confirmed, procurement will sign and upload the SOC2 report. Our procurement contact is procurement@finboard.com — they'll be on the DocuSign. Tight timeline for us: would like this live by the end of May.

Appreciate the help —
Anna
